title: When Men Use AI, They're Resourceful. When Women Use AI, They're Cheating.
tldr: Three studies show women are trusted less than men for identical AI use, a bias that shapes how AI adoption is perceived inside comms teams. It reframes an AI story as a workplace-trust and culture problem.
why_fresh: new research angle on AI-use bias
angle: Write about how perception bias around AI tools quietly reshapes who gets credit inside communications teams.

title: Marketers have bought into microdramas — but a lack of ROI might make them irrelevant
tldr: Microdramas are pulling brand dollars and real audiences, but nobody can prove they convert. A sharp case study on a hot format's attention-vs-measurement gap.
why_fresh: emerging format trend with fresh skepticism
angle: Analyze whether microdramas are a genuine content-consumption shift or a Quibi rerun in disguise.

title: In Graphic Detail: LLMs keep citing YouTube in search results
tldr: New data shows AI search engines lean heavily on YouTube videos, revealing how differently LLMs surface sources vs Google. Crucial for anyone rethinking content discoverability.
why_fresh: new data on LLM citation behavior
angle: Explore why video is becoming the currency of AI search visibility and what that means for content strategy.

title: The future of communications runs on trust. Here's what crisis leaders say matters now.
tldr: Crisis comms leaders argue everyday communications determine crisis outcomes in an era where AI fakes and Reddit complaints escalate in minutes. A timely reframing of crisis prep as continuous trust-building.
angle: Argue that crisis readiness is now a byproduct of daily narrative discipline, not a playbook you pull off the shelf.

title: Gap rolls out Fashiontainment strategy with boy band collaboration
tldr: Gap frames a boy-band tie-up as an ongoing content ecosystem — experiences, apparel and a documentary series — not a one-off campaign. A concrete breakdown of branded entertainment as omnichannel strategy.
why_fresh: campaign breakdown of new entertainment-content model
angle: Break down how brands are building multi-format content universes instead of campaigns.

title: AXA sharpens insurance push with human stories
tldr: AXA leans into real human narratives to sell insurance, a category usually drowning in jargon. A clean case study in human-centered storytelling over polish.
why_fresh: routine campaign but strong human-story angle
angle: Use AXA to show how humanizing a dry category outperforms polished corporate messaging.

title: Some creators want to negotiate deals like TV networks
tldr: Top creators are pushing for TV-network-style deal structures, signaling the creator economy's maturation into a formal media business. Relevant to how content and talent economics are shifting.
angle: Examine what it means when creators start behaving—and contracting—like media networks.

title: Now that's what I call comms planning! Taco Bell's 'Guacabono'
tldr: A breakdown of the strategic thinking behind Taco Bell's Guacabono stunt that's cutting through right now. Useful campaign anatomy for comms planners.
angle: Dissect what makes a comms-led stunt earn attention without a big media buy.

title: Stop asking AI to be creative. Ask it to be correct
tldr: Argues we've inverted AI's value by outsourcing the human, creative work while keeping the drudgery. A provocative reframe of how to divide labor with LLMs.
angle: Make the case that keeping the creative work human is a strategy, not nostalgia.

title: The Brand No Longer Belongs to Marketing. It Belongs to People Who Can Quit.
tldr: Provocative argument that employees—not marketing departments—now own brand meaning, since they can walk and speak out. Ties directly to employee-generated content and internal comms.
angle: Explore how employee agency has become the real locus of brand control.

title: AI Barely Uses Your Website to Describe Your Brand
tldr: Data suggests AI models describe brands using sources other than their own websites, upending owned-content assumptions. Important for content and GEO strategy.
why_fresh: new finding on AI brand representation
angle: Rethink owned-content strategy when AI ignores your website to describe you.

title: Employee Generated Content Platforms Ranked for Brand Safe Scale
tldr: A ranking of platforms enabling employee-generated content at scale with brand safety controls. Directly on Igor's high-priority EGC theme.
angle: Assess whether 'brand-safe scale' and authentic employee voice can truly coexist.

title: Mark Ritson: Even 10,000 synthetic Ritsons can't tell Anthropic the whole story
tldr: Ritson skewers the idea that synthetic personas or AI clones can replicate real human insight and taste. A sharp counter to synthetic-media hype.
angle: Argue why human taste stays uncopyable even as synthetic audiences proliferate.

title: Future of TV Briefing: Inside The Wall Street Journal's new shows strategy
tldr: WSJ is restructuring its podcast operation around video and social distribution. A concrete look at how a legacy outlet reshapes owned audio for a multi-format world.
angle: Unpack how newsrooms are rebuilding podcasts as video-first social properties.

title: Do Fashion Brands Need a Clipping Strategy?
tldr: Vogue examines how fashion brands turn runway and event moments into short shareable clips as a deliberate content discipline. A window into micro-content operations in a visual industry.
angle: Explore the 'clipping strategy' as a new content-ops discipline for visual brands.
